name: MonarchFlowLayout
title: Inline
summary: A horizontal row that wraps onto new rows when its children do not fit, with spacing from the Monarch space scale. SwiftUI's HStack does not wrap.
whenToUse: For rows of buttons, tags, badges or metadata that must not overflow a narrow screen or a large text size.
whenNotToUse: For a row that never needs to wrap use HStack. For equal columns use LazyVGrid or Grid (see grid). For a choice between a row and a column use ViewThatFits.
api: MonarchFlowLayout.init(spacing: CGFloat? = nil, rowSpacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: VerticalAlignment = .center, justification: MonarchFlowLayoutJustification = .leading)
enum MonarchFlowLayoutJustification { case leading, center, trailing, spaceBetween }

options.name: spacing
options.description: The space between children in a row. 8 points when nil. Take it from theme.spacing.

options.name: rowSpacing
options.description: The space between rows. Equal to spacing when nil.

options.name: alignment
options.description: How children of different heights line up in a row: top, center, bottom or a text baseline.

options.name: justification
options.description: leading, center, trailing or spaceBetween: where a row sits in the left-over width.

appearance: A layout draws nothing. Its children look the same in every theme as they do outside it.
platformNotes: The web's Inline is a flex row with wrap, align and justify. iOS has no wrapping stack, so Monarch ships this Layout; Android uses the platform FlowRow and ships nothing. The web's wrap={false} is HStack, and align="stretch" is not offered. With leading justification the layout is as wide as its widest row; with the others it fills the width it is offered.
accessibility: The layout adds no accessibility element; children keep their own.
Children are placed in source order, which is the order VoiceOver reads them in. Justification never reorders them.
Rows wrap instead of overflowing at large Dynamic Type sizes.
Positions are computed from the leading edge, so rows follow the layout direction.
edgeCases: A child wider than the layout gets a row of its own and is offered the full width, so text wraps.
With no width limit (inside a horizontal ScrollView or with fixedSize) everything is one row.
Negative spacing is treated as zero.
spaceBetween leaves a row with one child at the leading edge.
Spacer has no flexible length here; use justification.
